body.statement: For every fixed finite nonempty \(S\), the map in \(\mathrm{def{:}fzg\mbox{-}augmented\mbox{-}action}\) embeds the present holdout design in the two-stage selective-randomization action representation of Freidling, Zhao, and Gao: the first randomized action is the joint pair \((H,Z_1)\) with the known product mass displayed in that definition, the selector is \(C_n(\rho)\), and the stage--\(2\) recruitment and assignment kernel depends on the past through \(C_n(\rho)\).  At \(h=0\), sharp-zero imputability makes their Proposition~2 reference computable and that reference is exactly \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\); their Proposition~1 validity conclusion is exactly the conditional superuniformity in \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\mbox{-}selective\mbox{-}level}\).
body.proof_tex:
The random-holdout and stage--\(1\) complete-randomization assumptions give
\[
\mathsf P\{\mathcal A_{n,1}^{\mathrm{aug}}=a\}
=q_{n,1}^{\mathrm{aug}}(a)
\]
on the stated finite support, because the holdout and assignment are independent within each stratum and the strata are mutually independent.  The observed responses and the displayed selector formula make \(C_n(\rho)\) measurable after that action.  The stage--\(2\) assumption says exactly that, conditional on this history, the next action has the product mass in the definition and has coordinates only for selected strata.  Hence the chronological design has the required two-stage adaptive action factorization.

At \(h=0\), \(Y^{(0)}(1)=Y^{(0)}(0)=B\), so the sharp-null completion imputes every response needed to recompute the selector and rank statistic under every candidate action.  The explicit-support lemma proves that the same-selection actions are precisely \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{0,\rho},\rho)\).  Restricting the product action mass to this support and dividing by its positive mass gives exactly the formula defining \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\).  This verifies the computability premise and identifies the reference in the cited Proposition~2.  The finite-support tail calculation in the exact-level theorem then proves the same conditional superuniformity conclusion as cited Proposition~1.  Thus the mapping is an exact specialization for validity and computability.  The mapping itself contains no Gaussian approximation, local-power integral, discrepancy sign rule, or optimization argument; those conclusions come only from this note's separate transfer and frontier theorems.
body.justification: The proposition records the exact augmented-action map rather than relying on an informal resemblance.
body.gap: It identifies the inherited validity and computability layer while separating it from the new Gaussian frontier.
body.consumer: Readers can verify precisely which published selective-randomization result transfers.
